requirement: Convert strings, integers and Decimals to cent amounts rounded half up, reject floats, booleans, unparsable text and non-finite values, and split a total into a number of parts whose cents sum exactly.
skeleton: to_money validating the input type, parsing with Decimal, rejecting non-finite values and quantizing to CENT with ROUND_HALF_UP, and split_evenly distributing whole cents with divmod.
caption: Money handling with the standard-library decimal module. to_money(value) raises TypeError naming the unsupported money value type for anything that is not a str, int or Decimal, including bool and float, so binary floating-point error never enters an amount. It parses the value with Decimal, turning decimal.InvalidOperation into ValueError saying the text is not a number, raises ValueError saying it is not a finite amount for NaN or infinity, and quantizes to the module constant CENT of 0.01 with ROUND_HALF_UP. split_evenly(total, parts) raises ValueError saying parts must be at least 1 when parts is below one, converts the rounded total to a whole number of cents, uses divmod to find the base share and the leftover cents, and returns Decimal amounts where the first leftover parts get one extra cent, so the parts always add back to the total. The fixture asserts that 0.125 becomes 0.13, 2.675 becomes 2.68, the integer 3 prints as 3.00 and 1.004 becomes 1.00, that 0.1 and True raise TypeError, that 12,50 raises ValueError as not a number and NaN as not finite, that 1.00 in three parts is 0.34, 0.33 and 0.33, that four parts of 10.01 sum back to 10.01, and that zero parts raise ValueError.

plan.intent: Handle currency amounts without floating-point error
constraints: Only str, int and Decimal inputs are accepted; anything else raises TypeError
Amounts round half up to cents
Unparsable and non-finite values raise ValueError
Split parts sum exactly to the total with extra cents on the first parts
Fewer than one part raises ValueError

rationale.teaches: Decimal quantize with an explicit rounding mode, input type guarding against floats, and integer cent arithmetic for exact splits.
rationale.why: Money bugs come from floats, the default banker's rounding and lost cents in splits, and each only shows on specific half-cent and indivisible amounts.

ops.docstring: Money amounts as Decimal cents: reject floats, round half up, split exactly.

ops.stmt: from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation

ops.source:
def split_evenly(total: Decimal, parts: int) -> list[Decimal]:
    """Split total into cent amounts that sum exactly, extra cents going first."""
    if parts < 1:
        raise ValueError("parts must be at least 1")
    cents = int(to_money(total) / CENT)
    base, extra = divmod(cents, parts)
    return [Decimal(base + (1 if i < extra else 0)) * CENT for i in range(parts)]

candidates.why_wrong: Floats and booleans are converted directly, carrying binary rounding error into amounts.
quantize uses the context default of half-even rounding, so 0.125 becomes 0.12.
Leftover cents go to the last parts instead of the first.
Zero parts pass the check and fail with ZeroDivisionError instead of ValueError.
NaN reaches quantize and raises decimal.InvalidOperation instead of a ValueError.
